position: FERC: RTOs/ISOs and Electric Power Markets
proposal: The Mandate recommends that FERC reexamine whether regional transmission organizations still serve the public, require RTOs to return to market fundamentals so reliable dispatchable resources are properly valued (options named include backup requirements for intermittent bids, dual energy markets, or reliability markets in place of mixed capacity markets), end undue discrimination that lets subsidized resources distort prices, pass the benefits of renewables to customers, and affirm that states decide whether to join an RTO, possibly allowing non-RTO power pools.
remaining: A FERC finding or rulemaking on the premise of RTOs themselves (page 404)
Market rules that require intermittent resources to be backed by dispatchable supply, dual energy markets, or reliability markets (page 404)
Pass-through of renewable subsidy benefits to customers (page 404)
An affirmation that states decide RTO membership and allowance for non-RTO pools (page 405; none found)

review.mandate_note: Pages 404 to 405 ask FERC to reexamine whether RTOs serve customers, require RTOs to value reliable dispatchable resources (backup requirements, dual markets or reliability-only markets, alternatives to marginal price auctions), pass renewable subsidy benefits to customers, end subsidy-driven price distortion, and affirm that states choose whether to join an RTO, possibly with non-RTO pools.

sources.title: Meeting the Challenge of Resource Adequacy in RTO and ISO Regions; Third Supplemental Notice of Commissioner-Led Technical Conference
FERC Holds Technical Conference to Explore Resource Adequacy Challenges
FERC Directs Nation's Largest Grid Operator to Create New Rules to Embrace Innovation and Protect Consumers
FERC order of 2026-09-29, Docket ER26-3380 (PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement)

status_summary: On 2025-06-04 and 2025-06-05 FERC held a commissioner-led technical conference on resource adequacy in RTO and ISO regions, covering the role of capacity markets, alternatives such as long-term contracting, and the division of responsibility with states (docket AD25-7). On 2025-12-18 FERC found PJM's tariff unjust and unreasonable for lacking clear co-location rules, directed new transmission service options, and required PJM to report on faster capacity additions and its reliability backstop. On 2026-09-29 FERC accepted PJM's reliability backstop procurement filing, suspended it to 2027-02-28 subject to a paper hearing and opened docket EL26-108, and rejected a request to add valuation of dispatchable attributes, finding PJM's accreditation already captures them. No FERC action reexamining the RTO model, adopting the Mandate's dispatchable-valuation options or affirming state choice on RTO membership was found.

timeline.event: FERC held a two-day commissioner-led technical conference on resource adequacy in RTO and ISO regions (docket AD25-7), covering capacity markets, alternatives and the role of states; the second day was 2025-06-05.

FERC issued an order (docket EL25-49) finding PJM's tariff unjust and unreasonable for lacking clear co-location rules, directing new transmission service options for co-located load, and requiring PJM to report by 2026-01-19 on faster capacity additions and its reliability backstop.

FERC accepted PJM's reliability backstop procurement filing, suspended it to 2027-02-28 subject to refund and a paper hearing on cost allocation, transmission owner exit and collateral, opened section 206 docket EL26-108, and rejected a request to add dispatchable-attribute valuation to the selection method.

title: Reexamine RTO premise, value dispatchable resources, let states decide on RTO membership
uncertainties: The December 2025 order was read through the FERC news release, not the order text. No FERC action on states choosing RTO membership, on non-RTO pools, or on any rulemaking reexamining RTOs was found. The researcher searched FERC, PJM, Federal Register and law-firm sources; DOE section 403 directives on large loads were seen only through law-firm headlines and are not treated as events here. The FERC September 2026 commission meeting summary on ferc.gov listed no RTO market design item beyond tariff matters. The 2026-09-29 order is read from a copy hosted on pjm.com. Overlap with c12-07 on the PJM backstop is intentional; this record stays on market design.
